observed_state: Mid-game. Two of your Darkness Energy are already in the discard pile and the opponent is flipping Crushing Hammer heads. You have a Night Stretcher available and a turn in which you can play it. Munkidori’s Adrena-Brain works only while a Darkness Energy is attached to it.
full_record: The opponent flipped a third Crushing Hammer heads, discarded his third Darkness Energy, and used Budew plus Munkidori to lock him out. He lost the game.
unknown_fields: their remaining Crushing Hammer count and flips
what else the turn could have done
prompt: Do you play Night Stretcher now to put a Darkness Energy back in hand, before they can discard the third one?
criticality_source: Estimated from the source: Hedrick names this as the mistake that made the game very difficult.

choices.text: Play Night Stretcher now and recover a Darkness Energy pre-emptively
Hold Night Stretcher and use the turn otherwise

evidence.claim: Andrew Hedrick played this line in Worlds 2026, Swiss round 12, game 2. A pro’s choice is not proof it is best.
Hedrick did not play it and says he should have: the third Crushing Hammer heads then left him with all Darkness Energy in the discard and no way to stop their Munkidori loop.
Andrew Hedrick, reviewing his own game, judges B inferior; he says he "probably should have" played it, and the board is not described precisely enough to verify what the turn gave up.
The line he names instead: playing Night Stretcher earlier would have kept a Darkness Energy available after the third Crushing Hammer heads.
What else the turn could have done is unknown.
Crushing Hammer is a coin flip, so no line here is deterministic.

research_label.label: INACCURACY
research_label.why: The player says he "probably should have" played it; the board is not described precisely enough to verify what the turn gave up.
research_label.note: RESEARCH LABEL ONLY: not application truth, not imported as a verdict.
